title: Configurations and eligibility (registry/eligibility.yaml)
description: Which SoC configurations are registered (walked, T0-tested nightly, shown on the dashboard), which are frozen or silicon, and (Phase 4) which default branches the bot may auto-merge into. Changed only through a merge request to the registry's protected main. Owner: registry loader. B2, B5, D2, H1, E3, E5.

auto_merge.description: Phase 4 (E2, E3, E5). Component id -> change classes the bot may auto-merge into that component's default branch, once shadow mode has ended. Absent or empty in v1.

tiers_file.description: CR-12: registry `tiers.yaml` (optional), the local T1/T2 commands of each configuration (`nanosoc-rm compat CONFIG --tier t1|t2`, interfaces.md section 9a 'Tiers'). A configuration it names must be registered in eligibility.yaml (README section 3 rule 14). Additive optional file: no schema bump.

tier_command.description: One tier's command. It runs in a sandbox checkout of the configuration's resolved tree with a clean environment: PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, HOME and TMPDIR inside the sandbox, TREE = the checkout's root, NANOSOC_RM_TIER, NANOSOC_RM_VERDICTS (when `verdicts` is declared), then `env` in file order (`${NAME}` expands an earlier name; an unknown name is refused). Nothing else is inherited: no set_env.sh is ever sourced, and ARM_IP_LIBRARY_PATH is absent unless `env` names it.

command.description: An argv list (run as is), or a shell string (run with `bash --noprofile --norc -c`). Never sources a set_env.sh.

cwd.description: Tree-relative; `.` is the tree root. No absolute path, no `..`.

pins.description: The tree paths of the pins the command needs, each with its whole subtree (and the pins above it). Only these are laid out in the sandbox; absent = every pin of the tree.

budget_s.description: D1 budget for this command; over it = over_budget (a warning); killed at 1.5 x.

needs.description: vcs-seat: one local tier run at a time holds the host's seat lock (busy = INFRA). network: the command reaches a network (recorded, not enforced).

verdicts.description: Tree-relative path of the toolkit-format verdicts.tsv the command writes (removed before the run).

regenerates.description: The command regenerates build_soc: refused unless the caller sets NANOSOC_GEN_OK=1, which is then passed on.

regen_command.description: Wave D (interfaces.md section 20): the command that regenerates the configuration's generated output (build_soc) for `nanosoc-rm regen` and the C3/C7 class measurement. It runs as a tier_command does (same sandbox, clean environment, budget, kill at 1.5 x), always with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and under nice. The tool never sets a vendor-library variable: `env` may not name ARM_IP_LIBRARY_PATH or SOCLABS_DMA250_DIR, so the generator skips its vendor-rendered parts and the measurement records what it skipped under `coverage`.

command.description: An argv list (run as is), or a shell string (run with `bash --noprofile --norc -c`). Never sources a set_env.sh.

pins.description: As tier_command: only these pins (with their subtrees) are laid out.

budget_s.description: D1 budget of one render; killed at 1.5 x.

output.description: Tree-relative directory the command writes (deleted before the run); every file under it is the regenerated output.

include.description: Globs over paths relative to `output`; absent = every file.

exclude.description: Globs over paths relative to `output`, added to the tool's own (logs, __pycache__).

id.description: B2. Also the <config> segment of keep/<config>/<component> tags (C10).

component.description: B2: must be a catalogue component of class soc_ref or example.

ref.description: B2: the branch or tag on the component's canonical host.

commit.description: Required when frozen. The walker, B5 and T0 always use this commit for a frozen configuration, whatever `ref` says: `ref` is then informational. A TAG that stops peeling to it raises a tag_moved alert (C10); a branch that moves on raises nothing.

errata_prefix.description: F1, F4: the id prefix of this configuration's errata (ETH-R0P0 gives ETH-R0P0-ERR-001). Required once the configuration has an erratum (README section 3 rule 11).

silicon.description: B5, F1, F4, C10 (silicon/<chip>-rNpM). A silicon configuration is always frozen.

upgrade_from.description: D2 upgrade-path clone: the previous release to upgrade from. Absent -> gate t0.clone.upgrade-path records SKIP with the reason.

t0_waivers.description: D2, D6 (GATE2 Q1, approved 2026-10-01): known T0 failures of a FROZEN configuration that can never be fixed in its tree. Each covers one item of one gate (README section 6): the item is shown amber with its reason and approver, and a gate whose every non-pass item is covered rolls up WAIVED instead of FAIL or UNVERIFIED. Any other failure is still FAIL, so a new red on a frozen tree stays visible. The runner never sees waivers: verdicts.tsv and the items files are unchanged and the raw verdict is stored beside the waived one. A waiver that matched nothing in an accepted run raises a `waiver_unused` alert. Uniqueness and gate rules: README section 3 rule 13.

t0_waiver.description: One waived T0 item. Matches the item of `gate` at `tree_path` whose result is `result` (result-bundle.schema.json gate_item). A `not-reached` item below a covered item of the same gate is covered by it (it was not reached because of the waived item). No wildcards: each waiver names one item.

gate.description: A configuration gate that judges pins. Never t0.infra.probe or t0.runner.hardened (they judge the job, not the tree), never a t0.registry.* gate (the registry is not frozen), and never a gate's .negctl (D6: a control that did not fire is never waived).

reason.description: Why this item can never pass in this frozen tree, and what would retire the waiver.

approved_by.description: The login of the person who approved the waiver. The registry merge request is the record.

quality_file.description: CR-14 (Q1, Q2): registry `quality.yaml` (optional), the comment-density thresholds per language (comment ratio max_ratio, applied to files with at least min_lines non-blank lines), paths to exclude (fnmatch globs), the largest file read, and the age in days at which a TODO is stale. `components.<id>` overrides any of these for one component. Defaults apply where the file is silent (nanosoc_rm.quality.languages.DEFAULTS). Additive optional file: no schema bump.
